summary:
Outpost Odyssey is a browser-based space survival game that works as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Players command a crew building a permanent outpost at Artemis Base Alpha on the Moon or Ares Colony Prime on Mars. Each Sol (day), they balance oxygen, water, food, power, radiation shielding and crew health. They also respond to hazards such as solar storms, equipment failures and Martian dust storms. It includes a six-mission campaign, a free-play sandbox, three crisis challenges and a guided tutorial.

It addresses the challenge by turning real mission engineering into play. Life support, power storage and radiation protection are linked, so every decision has a trade-off. Live NASA DONKI space weather data raises or lowers the radiation hazard, and unlocked research reveals findings from NASA OSDR studies. An offline fallback archive keeps it working in classrooms.

It matters because it lets students experience why Artemis and Mars missions are engineered the way they are, with no login or install required.
details:
Project Details: Outpost Odyssey

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for the Moon and Mars
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

1. What does it do or how does it work?

Outpost Odyssey is an educational space survival and systems engineering simulation game where players take command of humanity's first permanent surface settlements at Artemis Base Alpha (Shackleton Crater, Moon) and Ares Colony Prime (Jezero Crater, Mars).

The game simulates closed-loop Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), power grids, and radiation shielding against authentic deep-space hazards. Each simulated Sol (day), players manage interdependent engineering trade-offs:

  • Life Support (ECLSS): Electrolyzing recycled water into breathable oxygen and scrubbing toxic CO2\text{CO}_2CO2​.
  • Power Grid: Balancing solar arrays and cryogenic battery reserves across the 354-hour (14-day) lunar night or multi-Sol Martian atmospheric dust slumps.
  • In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU): Sintering raw regolith into storm shelters and extracting subsurface ice crystals.
  • Radiation & Space Weather Countermeasures: Fortifying bunkers against ionizing radiation and deploying tactical countermeasures (e.g., pneumatically purging dust off solar arrays, sealing micro-fractures in water recovery loops, or rerouting circuit breakers).

The game connects to live NASA Heliophysics telemetry (DONKI) through a serverless function to calculate dynamic solar radiation hazards, backed by space biology experiments from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR).

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Demystifies Systems Engineering: Transforms abstract aerospace concepts (electrolysis, regenerative life support, radiation dosimetry, power storage) into visceral, cause-and-effect gameplay.
  • Fosters Critical Thinking & Trade-Off Analysis: Demonstrates that in space settlement, there are no frictionless solutions—boosting life support burns electricity, growing aeroponic crops demands scarce water, and saving battery reserves risks crew well-being.
  • 100% Zero-Barrier Classroom Accessibility: Runs directly in any modern web browser on laptops, Chromebooks, and tablets without logins, installs, or heavy downloads.
  • Built-in Resilient Offline Fallback: If an internet connection drops or the NASA API rate limit is reached, an embedded high-fidelity educational archive seamlessly activates so gameplay and learning never stall.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to ignite passion for STEM and human space exploration in students, educators, and the public. By stepping into the shoes of a flight director, learners transition from passive consumers of space facts to active problem-solvers who understand why Artemis and Mars missions are engineered the way they are. Our goal is to inspire the Artemis Generation to pursue careers in aerospace engineering, planetary geology, biology, and computer science.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Core Languages & Frameworks: React 19, TypeScript, and Vite 7 for high-performance, modular frontend rendering.
  • Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS with custom deep-space color palettes, responsive HUD layouts, and glassmorphism.
    • NASA DONKI (FLR, CME, GST endpoints) via api.nasa.gov.
    • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR studies OSD-379, OSD-120, OSD-473, OSD-254, OSD-514).
    • NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance & Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LROC) mission data.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Turning Real NASA Research into Direct Game Mechanics: Instead of generic sci-fi tropes, every technology in Outpost Odyssey corresponds to authentic NASA literature. Unlocking space biology research directly rewards players with OSDR experiment summaries (such as using narrow-band LED lighting on Arabidopsis root gravitropism or hydrogen-rich shielding to prevent lymphocyte chromosomal breakage).
  • Live Weather Integration with Fallback Narrative: Live solar activity in our solar system directly affects the player's shield decay and radiation risk in real time.
  • Tactical Autonomous Field Directives: Rather than simple menus, players can deploy surface rovers (VIPER or Perseverance), dispatch astronaut spacewalks, or run orbital remote sensing sweeps across actual lunar and Martian crater coordinates.
  • Sol Debrief Ceremonies: After every completed day, players receive a structured mission debrief with rotating NASA educational facts, crew status checkups, and telemetry graphs.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Scientific Accuracy vs. Gameplay Fun: Real life-support engineering involves differential equations and complex chemical balances. We distilled these physics into five readable, interdependent resource meters (Oxygen, Water, Food, Power, Shielding/Health) that maintain scientific fidelity while remaining engaging and fun for middle school to college students.
  • Planetary Realism (Moon vs. Mars): We explicitly modeled the contrasting survival constraints of both celestial bodies—Artemis Base Alpha faces the brutal 354-hour lunar night where battery storage is paramount, whereas Ares Colony Prime battles atmospheric dust accumulation on solar arrays and extreme water scarcity.
  • Universal Accessibility & Screen Bounds: Designed an adaptive UI ensuring zero clipping, responsive typography, and high-contrast color badges compliant with WCAG accessibility guidelines across mobile phones, tablets, and desktop displays.
  • Privacy & Classroom Safety: Requires zero user logins, stores game progression strictly on the local client (localStorage), and collects zero personal data.
